question: Can one exact historical scratch value be recursively regenerated without a full replay scratchpad inside the half-scratch byte model?

algorithm.primary_execution: direct-mapped cache plus exact written-word bitmap
algorithm.regeneration_key: packed 32-bit (stop iteration, word) identity with 15 word bits
algorithm.regeneration: replay machine state from genesis; recursively request every missing read at an earlier stop iteration; retain the requested target word across writes
algorithm.termination: every child stop is strictly less than its parent stop; stop zero returns the initial zero value
algorithm.memo: four-way set-associative exact values; deterministic replacement after all ways are occupied
algorithm.pilot_boundary: regenerate the first primary miss, retry it exactly, then refuse without a digest at the next miss

interpretation: successful reconstruction proves an exact value boundary, not a completed reduced-memory proof
the Python and C++ prototypes reserve logical frame bytes but do not yet measure compiler or interpreter stack and allocator overhead
the intentionally tiny primary cache gives regeneration structures most of the half-scratch arena and is not a throughput-optimized split
